humanities_role_explanation: Humanities disciplines (History, Literature & Arts, Philosophy, Law, etc.) are a minority of items (e.g., History 674, Literature and Arts 1,676, Philosophy 347) within a 285-subfield graduate-level multiple-choice knowledge/reasoning benchmark dominated by STEM (77.2%). The competence tested is general graduate-level knowledge and reasoning, not humanities disciplinary competence specifically.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only multiple-choice questions; image-dependent questions were explicitly excluded via a multimodal exclusion check.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Graduate-level multiple-choice questions (4-10 options, avg 9.67) across 285 subfields testing 'knowledge and reasoning'; 42.33% require mathematical calculation or formal reasoning; easy/middle splits reflect factual knowledge mastery and hard splits reasoning.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-discipline benchmark covering 13 disciplines, 72 fields, 285 subfields.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 51 models: 6 reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1, o1, o3-mini, QwQ), 28 chat models (GPT-4o, Claude-3.5, Gemini-2.0-flash, Qwen, Llama, etc.), 17 base models (plus more in the appendix).

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy at sample, subfield, field and discipline levels; also SD, CV and high-low group difference for discrimination analysis.

summary: SuperGPQA is a 26,529-question multiple-choice benchmark spanning 285 graduate-level disciplines, built via a human-LLM collaborative pipeline of expert source screening, crowd transcription and three-stage quality inspection. It evaluates 51 LLMs, with the best (DeepSeek-R1) reaching 61.82% accuracy.
key_findings: DeepSeek-R1 61.82% overall accuracy, o1-2024-12-17 60.24%; instruction tuning helps greatly (DeepSeek-V3 47.40 vs. Base 32.14); stronger models are more balanced across difficulty; humanities (History CV=0.175) discriminate more between top models than STEM; newer model versions score higher.
facets_explanation: Experts collect questions with solutions from textbooks and exercise websites; crowd annotators (undergraduate/master's students) transcribe, translate and convert them into multiple-choice format, with LLM-assisted distractor generation. Suspicious items are re-annotated by PhD-level experts. Answers are scored by single-letter match; a unique correct answer is required, and the paper treats ambiguity as a defect to remove. Some questions were supplemented from existing benchmarks.
results_explanation: DeepSeek-R1 scores 61.82 overall (sample-level accuracy); easy/middle/hard splits are 63.59/63.63/56.87, a gap of about 7 points for that model. The largest difficulty gap is Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct 44.82 (easy) vs 19.97 (hard), about 25 points. The input comparison (with vs. without subfield info) gives about 1 point (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct 41.93 vs 40.82). No human baseline is reported.

humanities_role.quote: Despite the relatively smaller representation of non-STEM disciplines (e.g., Philosophy: 347, Literature: 1,676, History: 674 questions)

dataset_size.quote: With 26,529 questions spanning 13 disciplines, 72 fields, and 285 subfields

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: Reasoning models and chat models are evaluated using a zero-shot approach, while base models are assessed using a five-shot evaluation.

gold_source.quote: Example problems with solutions from textbooks.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Context-dependent reasoning requiring real-world knowledge synthesis.

answer_multiplicity.quote: There is only one correct answer.
